intro: Professionals and everyday users convert atmospheres (atm) to psi (psi) when working across other and imperial standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One standard atmosphere equals 14.695949 psi, while 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.068046 atmospheres. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between atm and psi. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many psi (psi) are in 1 standard atmosphere (atm)?
faqs.answer: There are 14.69594878 psi (psi) in 1 standard atmosphere (atm), which rounds to 14.6959 psi for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pounds per square inch equals 0.068046 atmospheres.

faqs.question: How do I convert atmospheres to psi (atm to psi)?
faqs.answer: To convert atmospheres to psi, use the formula: psi = atm × 14.69594878. For example, converting 2.2 atm gives 32.3311 psi.

faqs.question: What is 2.2 atmospheres in psi?
faqs.answer: 2.2 atmospheres (atm) equals exactly 32.3311 psi (psi) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
